pts, 146 receipt lines |
| 3PL `outbound.csv` | 37,331 outbound lines (keyed order or shipment/item code) |
| QuickBooks `vendors.csv` | 11 vendors |
| `supplier_docs` commercial invoices (41 of the 135 PDFs) | read only for the product crosswalk |

## Crosswalk
There are 49 product hubs, one per SKU code. Each carries:
- **Shopify:** 49 variant IDs. 43 are exact and 6 are normalized at 0.9.
- **UPC:** 49 UPCs, which come from the Shopify barcodes.
- **3PL:** 49 item codes, matched exactly (1.0) on UPC.
  - The 3PL's own Client SKU is blank on 6 items and mistyped on others, such as BKL for BLK and SVL for SLV. I used the UPC and left Client SKU out of the match.
- **Factory:** 49 factory item codes, 49 suppliers and 49 HS codes, from the commercial invoices at 0.7. Descriptions agree one-to-one, and no other code carries the same description.
- **Amazon:** 25 listings, each pointing at its hub and ASIN. 14 are exact and 11 carry the `-FBA` suffix (normalized, 0.9). No two listings share an ASIN or a SKU.
- **Unmatched:** none.

I wrote the hubs under the regular `AH-XXX-NNNN-CCC` spelling. The 6 irregular Shopify codes are:
- `AH-CTB-16-LRG`
- `AHUTN0017NAT`
- `AH-TRY-18-NAT`
- `ah-btl-0020-blk`
- `AH-JAR-22-STL`
- `AH-TPT-23-CLR`

QuickBooks vendors map to the 8 supplier codes by company name, matched exactly. The forwarder, the customs broker and the 3PL have no supplier code, so they are indexed under `quickbooks/vendor` alone.

## Attributes registered
None. The installed vocabulary covered every ID and join key.

## Duplicate customers
I wrote 154 `core/same_as` links among Shopify customers:
- **Same mailbox after dropping the plus-alias:** 86 links at 0.9. There were no exact-mailbox matches. All the pairs have the same name.
- **Same full name and postal address:** 68 more links at 0.7. These are mostly one person's mailbox at two providers. I read ten of these against the source and all looked like the same person.
- **Cluster sizes:** 148 pairs and 3 triples. No account has more than two others pointing at it.

## Step 7 checks
- **Bare records from join keys:**
  - The only bare records are the 26 PO numbers named by 3PL receipts. These are expected, because the ingestion skill fills them in.
  - 33 receipt lines have a blank PO reference. I wrote no PO link for them.
  - 14 lines carry three POs in one field. I split those into separate links.
- **Counts:** every kind of record matches its source's distinct IDs.
- **Joins:** all 3PL outbound references resolved to a Shopify order name or an FBA shipment.

## Left out of the catalogue
- **QuickBooks `transaction_list_by_vendor.csv`:** it is the general ledger, so it is never indexed.
- **WeChat chats, the ops inbox and the other 94 supplier PDFs:** these are ingestion's. The PDFs are proformas, inspection reports and other documents.
- **3PL container and ASN numbers:** I left them out, because containers are reused across shipments and shipments are ingestion's.
- **Amazon orders:** they carry no customer ID, so none are linked to customers.

## Where the sources disagree on a term
- **SKU:**
  - Amazon's SKU is a listing code, sometimes with an `-FBA` suffix.
  - The 3PL's Client SKU is hand-typed and has typos and blanks.
  - Shopify's SKU has six irregular spellings.
  - I did not store the 3PL's or Shopify's variants. Our own code is the hub, and Amazon's spelling is kept on the listing.
- **Stock on hand:**
  - The 3PL splits it into on hand, allocated, available and damaged.
  - Shopify's `inventoryQuantity` equals the 3PL's Available.
  - Amazon splits stock into fulfillable, unsellable and reserved.
  - None of these quantities are stored.

## Left for you to decide
- Whether the 68 name-and-address duplicate links at 0.7 are acceptable. They would be 0.9 if you count that as strong evidence.
- Whether to index the three non-factory QuickBooks vendors under supplier codes.

Field authority is recorded on the Shopify, Amazon, 3PL and QuickBooks identifiers.

ingest.final:
I ingested everything: 48 proformas, 41 invoice/packing-list pairs, 46 inspection reports, the 8 WeChat chats and all 163 emails. It came to 422 transactions, written in issue order, and the store accepted all of them without errors.

None of these documents had been read before, so nothing was skipped. The store only held the catalogue's reads of the invoices for item and HS codes.

**Created or updated**
- **Purchase orders:** 48, of which 22 are new. They have 196 lines.
- **Suppliers:** 8, with name, address, incoterm, payment terms, currency and port.
- **Inspections:** 46.
- **Shipments:** 32, each created from its booking. All 31 house bills are attached to those booking entities, so nothing is duplicated.
- **Shipment lines:** 166.
- **Customs entries:** 30.
- **Documents:** 431 now have a URL and issue date.

PO status now stands at 37 received, 4 shipped, 5 in production, 1 ready and 1 confirmed.

**Facts below confidence 1**
- **0.9:**
  - ETD changes from chat, 18 of them. Dates carry no year, and some name the order by the supplier's PI number.
  - Container numbers from chat, 15. The message names no PO, so I took the supplier's PO that had passed inspection and not yet sailed.
  - "In production" after a deposit acknowledgement, 43. The reply names no PO, so I matched it to the deposit it answers. For deposits that name no PO, I matched the amount to the PI total times the deposit share.
- **Treated as acknowledgements:** two plain "OK" replies right after a deposit message (Sunny on 2026-03-29, Amy on 2026-03-31). Each was followed minutes later by a proper acknowledgement.
- **Chat times:** converted as New York time. Supplier dates were read as China dates.

**Unresolved**
- **Voice notes:** the `[语音]` messages can't be read.
- **Last two orders:** PO-2026-0029 has no deposit acknowledgement yet. PO-2026-0023 is ready, with its ETD slipped to 1 October and nothing shipped.
- **HS codes:** all invoice HS codes match the SKUs.
- **Contact names:** left out, because no attribute is cleared for personal data.
- **Inspector name:** stored as "Linkcheck Inspection Services", the title-cased form of the report's all-caps header. The brand's real casing isn't in any document.
- **Warehouse receipts:** 74 lines show damaged or short counts (no attribute for them). The largest shortfalls are:
  - **PBLHB2500005:** AH-BWL-0015-CLY expected 1680, received 1656.
  - **TGHU7372239:** AH-TMB-0019-BLK expected 576, received 552.

**Gaps in the vocabulary (left in the documents)**
- **Price changes:**
  - Mingjia: +3% from 1 March.
  - Qisheng: +4% from 1 May.
  - Lanxin: +5% from 15 August.
  - Hetai: −2% from 1 July.
- **Payments:** deposit and balance amounts.
- **Samples:** DHL sample courier numbers.
- **Holiday closures:** the Chinese New Year and National Day notices.
- **Quotes:** requests for quotes on new colours and next year's catalogue.
- **Warehouse counts:** the received and damaged counts above.

rerun.final:
This was a re-run on unchanged sources, so I wrote nothing to the store and made no changes. The checks found nothing wrong.

**Sources**
- I compared the SHA-256 of every indexed export file with the hash the store holds for it. All of them match.
- The store already holds the full catalogue:
  - 26,546 Shopify orders and 37,773 order lines
  - 21,129 customers
  - 38,264 Amazon orders and 43,513 order lines
  - 25 Amazon listings and 25 ASINs
  - 37,331 3PL outbound lines and 146 receipt lines
  - 29 receipts and 49 FBA shipments
  - 49 product hubs
  - 11 QuickBooks vendors
- The distinct IDs I re-counted in the sources match these counts for Shopify orders, order lines and customers, Amazon orders, listings and order lines, and 3PL outbound rows.
- **Not indexed on purpose:**
  - `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv` is the general ledger, which is never indexed.
  - `3pl/inventory_snapshot.csv` and `amazon/fba_inventory.txt` hold stock levels, not IDs or join keys. The store has no document entry for either.
  - The PDFs, WeChat chats and ops inbox mbox belong to the ingestion skill. I did not touch them.
- `shopify/products.jsonl` has 73 lines and the store has 49 product hubs. I did not re-check that gap this run, so it is open.

**Step 7 checks**
- **Bare records:**
  - These are expected: they are records that other records name.
  - 38,264 Amazon orders, 20,975 Shopify customers, 25 ASINs and 49 FBA shipment IDs hold only their own ID.
  - 3 QuickBooks vendors are the carrier, the customs broker and the 3PL. They are not suppliers.
  - 10 receipts have no `receipt/po` yet, waiting for ingestion.
  - I found no malformed IDs: no blanks, lists or odd spellings.
- **Duplicates:**
  - There are 154 `core/same_as` links: 84 match on a normalized mailbox and 70 on the same name and address.
  - I checked all 154 against the orders and every one has a real shared mailbox or name and address. None is a different person.
  - No account has more than three others pointing at it.
- **Excised people:** I did not check this on this run.

I have nothing to propose and nothing for you to decide.
